projects.title: Tech Room Rebuild - Redesign of the DC supporting both the company's campus network and the infrastructure delivering Terminal Services to the public

description.text:

projects.title: Review and Redesign of 2014 Network Deployment Project - Changed End User requirements
projects.subtitle: Jul 2015 - Jul 2015

description.text:
▪ Expansion of original network to support 500 more access connections.
▪ Designed and planned implementation of access switch system with Cisco Stacking technology
▪ Temporarily activated "legacy" portion of the infrastructure through 8 Allied Telesys 10/100 switch to
serve the campus (will eventually be replaced by Cisco Stacking Switches)
▪ Rewrote Allied Telesys configuration to support Voice endpoints in the new office areas and
connection with Leaf/Spine portion of the network
▪ 100 Phone Endpoints provisioning and E1/PRI Trunk configuration for direct extension access
(each extension is reachable by PSTN through a direct number)

Telesys) since switches are not CDP/LLDP compatible and thus unable to assign Voice VLANs

VLAN ID on each of them.

projects.title: Cisco Ironport Mail Filtering Infrastructure Migration
projects.subtitle: Mar 2015 - Mar 2015

description.text:
▪ Pre-Existing Configuration analysis and migration from Ironport C160 Appliance (pre-Cisco Merger)
with brand new Cisco ESA C170 physical appliance.
▪ Analysis and re-design of Content Filtering rules to remove overlaps and false positives.
▪ Geographical Cut-Over between Rome and Milan nodes and preparation of new appliances for
each.
Issues encountered and applied solutions
▪ End user did not have a centralized SMA appliance but needed 1 year worth of MessageTracking
logs for auditing purposes.
▪ Cisco does not support MessageTracking log migration from a standalone ESA appliance. Only
migration path supported is through a SMA appliance.
▪ Solution
▫ Performed reverse-engineering on legacy Ironport Appliance
▫ Developed custom software solution based on python to procedurally export MessageTracking
Data in .csv format with _no support_ from the vendor.
▫ Succesfully exported over 20 million records (individual email tracking) and exposed them inside
a searchable database.

projects.title: High Availability E1 - SIP Gateway
projects.subtitle: Dec 2014 - Dec 2014

description.text:
The activity involved connecting 2 E1 connections on redundant Cisco ISR2921 voice gateways and
to expose the PSTN access as a single SIP session to the IVR system.
An active/passive solution was developed leveraging the Cisco platform and EEM scripting in
particular.
▪ SIP Session exposed on a Virtual IP through HSRP
▪ E1 Line status is monitored through custom EEM scripts
▪ HSRP instance priority is altered automatically as soon as E1 Line Status changes
▫ If E1 link is lost, the HSRP instance priority gets immediately lowered
▫ The SIP session relocates immediately on the secondary ISR (which will have a working E1
connection)

projects.title: High Volume Fax Server Deployment
projects.subtitle: Jun 2014 - Jun 2014

description.text:
Designed and implemented a Fax Server solution through opensource technologies
▪ Receiving and Archival of large volumes of fax messages
▪ 5000 faxes/months, 2500-3000 of which in a 7 days time frame every month
▪ Fax Lines: 2x ISDN BRI (4 channels total)
▪ Fax Reception handled by high performance DSP card managed by a Hylafax server Daemon. An
AvantFax WebUI was used for presentation.
▪ Configuration of a mail gateway to send/receive faxes through email.
▪ Automatic copy of received faxes on a Windows Network Share.
▪ Supported delivery through virtual printer. Users select a virtual printer from any windows
application (MS Word, Excel, Email etc.) and they are asked a phone number to send the
document to.

projects.title: Development of a Visualization system for Power production data
projects.subtitle: May 2014 - May 2014

description.text:
Client is a player in the clean energy market and requested a system to display stats for their energy
production infrastructure for promotional purposes in their Rome HQ.
Data is handled by a third-party info provider that gathers it from the power plants through SCADA and
then sells the access to the data and metric tracking to the company.
Said info-provider declined to give us API access to the raw data so that we could easily track power
production and display it on our own systems.
We then developed a custom Python app based on Selenium WebDriver that emulates a genuine HTTP user session and:
▪ Parses the HTML pages on the info-provider portal in which data is presented
▪ Extracts metrics requested by the end user
▪ Stores them in an internal DB
▪ A Web frontend gathers the data and displays them on a 100"​ Videowall panel inside the client's
HQ Reception.
Technologies employed:
▪ Selenium WebDriver
▪ Python
▪ Apache WebServer
▪ Custom PHP/Javascript frontend

projects.title: Complete Implementation of a Datacenter POD for a Video Surveillance and Law Enforcement Systems Integrator Product
projects.subtitle: Apr 2014 - Apr 2014

description.text:
▪ Full Compute, Storage, Network stack (meant to operate isolated from rest of datacenter)
supporting a custom application to archive remote video streams + metatadata (positioning,
timestamp, etc) from roughly 1000 mobile surveillance endpoints.
Compute
▪ 1 Windows 2012 Server for centralized backups and as a management console for all the system's
components
▪ 4 CentOS Baremetal Servers accessing a FibreChannel shared storage for video archiving.
Storage
▪ Design and Configuration of a Fibre Channel Fabric
▫ 2 Storage Processor
▫ 4 Client Nodes
▫ 2 Multipath discrete paths (active/active redundancy on the storage data path)
▪ Setup FC Switch Brocade 300
▪ SAN Zoning
▪ First activation and LUN provisioning array Dell MD3xxx
Network
▪ Configuration of Top of Rack Switch Dell ForceConnect 55xx in a stack
▫ setup link MLAG for active/active redundancy of every node
▪ Configured LACP bonding on both CentOS and Windows machines
▪ CentOS Hosts only exposed the application's web service to the "public"​ VLAN. Management and
configuration access restricted to the "private" VLAN.
The whole project was delivered with extreme time contraints (end user presented the project to us 5 days from final delivery with considerable economical penalties for them for a missed deadline) at the customer site.

projects.title: Edge Networking Rebuild and Virtualization Deployment
projects.subtitle: Mar 2014 - Mar 2014

description.text:
▪ Redesigned Internet termination for the site ( roughly 500 users, centralized Campus with in-house
web services and two branch offices). Replaced aging PIX515 with new ASA5512-X platform.
▪ Complete rework of the access policies (VPN, Web and ACLs)
▪ 0-downtime Cut-Over between PIX and ASA.
▪ Virtualized a few key services in a previously completely bare metal organization (introduced
VMware ESXi virtualization)
▪ Proof of Concept implementation for monitoring system based on Cisco Prime Infrastructure 2.0
(Created VMs, preliminary populated inventory with devices, trained end user's IT staffers)
▪ Partial redesign of the Layer 2 network (previously a flat /16 network, introduced two VLANs for the
two largest traffic categories and setup InterVLAN routing on ASA).
▪ Implemented a DNS filtering system based on blacklists on Cisco ASA
▪ Created a PHP/Python Front-End to add/remote filters procedurally from the ASA, allowing non-
Cisco trained staffers to operate the system without third-parties and with minimal risk for
disruption.

projects.title: Ephemeral Public Access WiFi Network
projects.subtitle: Mar 2014 - Mar 2014

description.text:
▪ Design and build of an ephemeral (4 days) Wired/Wireless network to support the national
conference of the organization inside ERGIFE Meeting Center in Rome.
▪ The network had to support check-in operations for guests ( 8 sign-in desks), the temporary
Operations office and customized SSIDs for guests with private traffic and segregation from the
meeting center internal network.
▪ User traffic was kept private by linking back to Organization HQ through VPN and egressing the
whole venue wifi traffic out of the HQ (customer's guest traffic never traversed the Meeting Center
network in cleartext).

projects.title: Network Design and Implementation
projects.subtitle: Mar 2014 - Mar 2014

description.text:
▪ Acted as pre-sales for Wired/Wireless network infrastructure upgrade.
▪ Designed the new wired and wireless network and planned migration from legacy infrastructure.
▪ Implemented a Leaf/Spine topology (Equal Cost Layer 2 setup) based on a Cisco 4500-X VSS
Spine and a Cisco WLC 5508 Wireless system. Estimated users: 1200
▪ Configured VSS for redundancy purposed and Multi-chassis Link Aggregation (MLAG).
▪ Implemented Leaf/Access layer with Cisco Catalyst 3560-X e 3560C switches.
▪ Drafted option for WPA Enterprise deployment leveraging ActiveDirectory for user authentication.

projects.title: Microsoft Terminal Services Server Farm Migration
projects.subtitle: Feb 2014 - Feb 2014

description.text:
The whole design and implementation was delivered within 5 days due to severe time constraints of
the end user.
The activity involved
▪ Complete activation of 2 physical servers and implementation of VMware ESXi hypervisor software
on them (from packaged to serving content in 48 hours)
▪ Established bidirectional trust between AD domains (across NAT, inside a VPN with no support
from the source Datacenter staff) to migrate 2000 users with no password changes required.
▪ Standing up of new Terminal Services farm and clearing of CAL RDP licensing with Microsoft
▪ Migrated a large number of SQL Server DBs (1500) for a total of 600 gbs between Turin and Rome
datacenters.
▪ Reimported DBs procedurally through T-SQL/Python scripts in order to minimize human error and
to check data integrity.
▪ Activated custom Fiscal application to be served over Terminal Services and developed GPOs to
minimize attack surface (only the application is presented to the 600 remote sites across Italy).
▪ Project started the 19th of February. At 11AM on Monday the 24th, the farm was already serving
content to 200 users.
